title: UDX: match libudx's own timing and SACK limits
description:
Follow-up to !26211. Three constants disagreed with libudx's own, reported by James Thomas of the libudx team.

libudx floors its retransmission timeout at one second rather than the two hundred milliseconds assumed here, so a repeat arriving between those two figures was reported as a timeout firing when no timeout could have fired.

The pause that suggests a tail loss probe, when no round trip time has been measured, was ten milliseconds. libudx schedules that probe a second out in the same situation, so the same figure now serves for both and the separate constant is gone. A repeat too soon to be either timer is now left as a plain retransmission rather than being attributed to a timer that did not fire.

Selective acknowledgement blocks were capped at thirty-two, which is what fits in the area data_offset can delimit. A packet carrying no payload leaves that byte zero and its blocks run to the end of the datagram instead, and libudx sends up to fifty of them that way. Blocks past the thirty-second were being dropped.

Adds two captures and two tests covering the cases above.

notes.body: No offense to your protocol, but I think I might prefer that the udx test captures be moved to a subdirectory in the test captures folder.

Three constants disagreed with the reference implementation, found in review
by James Thomas.

libudx floors its retransmission timeout at one second rather than the two
hundred milliseconds assumed here, so a repeat arriving between those two
figures was reported as a timeout firing when no timeout could have fired.

measured, was ten milliseconds. libudx schedules that probe a second out in
the same situation, so the same figure now serves for both and the separate
constant is gone. A repeat too soon to be either timer is now left as a plain
retransmission rather than being attributed to a timer that did not fire.

Selective acknowledgement blocks were capped at thirty-two, which is what fits
in the area data_offset can delimit. A packet carrying no payload leaves that
byte zero and its blocks run to the end of the datagram instead, and libudx
sends up to fifty of them that way. Blocks past the thirty-second were being
dropped.

Adds two captures and two tests covering the cases above.
